newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan changes law to allow stock option schemes.
newsitem.headline: Japan changes law to allow stock option schemes.

text.p: Japan changed the law on Friday to allow firms to buy back up to 10 percent of their own shares for use in stock option schemes for employees and executives.

The Upper House of parliament passed a bill revising the commercial code after the legislation won Lower House approval last week. Stock options give holders the right to buy shares at a set price within a certain period.
The change will take effect from June 1.

Under the old system Japan only allowed venture companies to have stock options, which are popular in the United States and Europe. Firms have been eager to have the rule relaxed in order to have greater flexibility in linking pay with performance.
Traditional Japanese compensation schemes tied to seniority have done little to reward corporate high-flyers and hence, critics say, provided scant incentive to achieve exceptional performance.
Japanese media have reported that major companies such as auto giant Toyota Motor Corp and chipmaker Fujitsu Ltd are set to introduce stock option programmes.

The revision will also enable firms to adopt share repurchase schemes without having to get the go-ahead from their annual shareholder meetings. The new law allows the firms to proceed with the schemes with only the approval of their board of directors.
